title: Track A — Foundations
summary: How to read a problem, derive the complexity you need before writing any code, and the C++ you actually use under a one-second limit. Includes a proper treatment of OOP — classes as invariants, RAII, the rule of 0/3/5 — and an honest section on when *not* to use it in a contest.
metaTitle: Foundations — approach, complexity, C++ and OOP
metaDescription: Problem-solving method, complexity analysis, competitive C++ and object-oriented design done properly.

title: Track B — Data structures from scratch
summary: Every structure built as a class, against an interface, with its invariant stated up front. You will not reach for `std::stack` until you have written one. Each lesson follows the same shape: the problem it solves, the invariant, the implementation, the complexity table, the pitfalls, and the problems that need it.
metaTitle: Data structures from scratch in C++
metaDescription: Dynamic arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, hash tables, trees, heaps, tries, graphs, DSU and range structures — each implemented as a class.

title: Track C — Patterns and problems
summary: The fourteen shapes that most interview problems reduce to. Problems attach to patterns rather than to a flat list, because recognising the shape is the part that transfers — a solved problem you cannot classify teaches you almost nothing.
metaTitle: Patterns — two pointers to dynamic programming
metaDescription: Two pointers, sliding window, binary search on the answer, monotonic stacks, backtracking, graph traversal, DP, greedy and bit manipulation.
